 ORDER

The Writ Petition has been filed in the nature of Certiorarified Mandamus, seeking interference with the order passed by the second respondent/the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration, Government of Tamil Nadu, Chennai, dated 08.10.2021 in R.No.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7460-4/2021/S9/FSSA and also the order of the third respondent/the Designated Officer, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department,
Food Safety Wing, Pudukottai, in R.No.513-4 (Kalai)/A1/FSSA/2021 and consequential Emergency Prohibition Notice, dated 04.10.2021, issued by the third respondent and to set aside all the above orders.
2.The petitioner claims that they are selling tobacco leaves in the name of Kalaiman Pugaiyilai for the past several decades.
They further claim that their brand has attained an unique identity.
They sell the tobacco to a large number of villagers in the State of Tamil Nadu.
They cut the tobacco in various sizes.
They choose various tobacco leaves and the tobacco leaves undergo cutting to establish unique features and special identity.
They claim that they sell unmanufactured tobacco leaves to the customers without any additives.
They claim that the products do not come under prohibited food products and under the Regulation 2.4.3 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and restriction on sales) Regulations 2011.

sentences.text:
It is contended that the products which the petitioner sold,
are processed tobacco, coming https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis under the category of food.

They are commonly called 'chewing tobacco'.
4.With respect to the issue of chewing tobacco, a learned Single Judge of this Court in Jeetmal Ramesh Kumar Vs. The Commissioner, Food Safety and Drug Administration Department and others, 2019 SCC online Mad 18993, had categorically held, after examining, the facts and the law that chewing tobacco is a food, since, it is in essence, as the word suggests, put in the mouth,
chewed, digested and therefore, it can be categorized as a food.

entities.text: Jeetmal Ramesh Kumar Vs. The Commissioner, Food Safety and Drug Administration Department and others, 2019 SCC online Mad 18993
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5.The learned Single Judge also placed reliance on a judgment of another learned Single Judge,
which the petitioner herein, also relies and a copy of which had been filed along with the typed set of papers, namely, the order of a learned Single Judge, dated 09.06.2017, in W.P.No.21 of 2017,
Jayavilas Tobacco Traders LLP, represented by its Partner Vs. Designated Officer Food Safety and Drugs Control Department.

sentences.text: However, the learned Single Judge was of the opinion that the reasoning of the learned Single Judge in Jayavilas case had been interfered with and overruled by a Division Bench of this Court, in J.Anbazhagan, Member of Legislative Assembly, Chepauk Vs. Union of India, reported in 2018 (4) MLJ 129.

This judgment of the Division Bench had been affirmed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in E.Siva Kumar Vs. Union https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of India,
reported in 2018 (7) SCC 365.
6.In paragraph No.12 of the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petition

entities.text: E.Siva Kumar Vs. Union https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the petitioner had very clearly stated that they mix jaggery water at the farm level and this is done in order to prevent the tobacco leaves from breaking or getting brittle.
It is also claimed that mixing of jaggery has been approved by the World Health Organization as well as by the Central Tobacco Research Industries for controlling and managing pests.

7.However, this process of mixing jaggery water and claiming relief on that account or relief for rather concession on that account had come up for consideration in State of Madras Vs. Bell Mark Tobacco Company, reported in 1967 (19) SCC 129 (SC).

entities.text: State of Madras Vs. Bell Mark Tobacco Company, reported in 1967 (19) SCC 129 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court was examining the sales tax imposed on tobacco and on chewing tobacco.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, thereafter,
held as follows:
'The Sales Tax tribunal has set out the process of preparation of chewing tobacco.
Raw tobacco is purchased under a transport permit issued by the Central Excise Department and there is warehoused in different lots.
Jaggery water or plain water is sprinkled on the bundles of tobacco and tobacco is allowed to ferment for about 40 days.
Heat is thereby generated and the tobacco gets well processed.
Stalks of t o b a c c o a r e b r o k e n a n d r e m o v e d , a n d s a n d a n d d u s t a r e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis removed.
After payment of excise duty the bundles of tobacco are brought to the premises of the factory, where chewing tobacco is prepared.
Jaggery juice is sprinkled on tobacco, and it is then cut into thin strips by shearing machines.
The resulting tobacco is called nice tobacco.

This nice tobacco M/S.S.M.Mohammed Ibrahim & Co. Private ... vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 20 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63832338/

sentences.text: Then flavouring essences are sprinkled on it and it is then packed in special wrappers.
The packets are known as chewing tobacco packets.
A large number of workmen are employed to carry out these several processes.

In the view of the High Court the cumulative effect of the various processes, such as soaking in jaggery water, shredding of tobacco and addition of flavouring essences to which tobacco was subjected before it was sold, amounted to a manufacturing process and the product sold was a manufactured product from raw tobacco purchased by the respondents.

We are in complete agreement with the view of the High Court on this part of the case.'
8.The facts are thus settled.
They have not been re-examined by any Court.

9.There was yet another judgment of the Supreme Court, in the case of State of Madras Vs.
M.N.A.AAbdul Rahiman, reported in 1967 (19) STC 134, which followed this judgment.

Bharat Agencies Vs. State of Telangana, had very categorically held that 'chewing tobacco is a food and which comes under one of the prohibited materials or food materials under the Regulation 2.3.4 of Food Safety and Standards(Prohibition and Restriction on Sales) Regulations 2011'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Division Bench of the Telangana High Court had examined the issue in entirety and had also stated that 'food' means any substance whether processed, partially processed or unprocessed, which is intended for human consumption and also includes primary food.

11.These judgments, to a large extent, settle the issue whether the product manufactured by the petitioner can be categorized as a food and since it is categorized as a 'food' and since it contains tobacco, whether it can be categorized as a 'prohibited food item'.
That issue is settled by the flow of judgments.

12.One point which is taken up by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner is that the initial notice was issued by the Designated Officer/the Tamil Nadu Food Safety Department, Pudukkottai to the petitioner herein, calling upon the petitioner to stop the manufacturing and selling of Kalaiman tobacco and to comply with FSS Rules and Regulations.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Food Safety Department, Pudukkottai
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: An answer was given https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis by the petitioner to this particular notice by the Designated Officer.
The impugned order had, however, been passed by the Commissioner of Food Safety.

This fact of another authority passing the order had been quite seriously questioned by the learned Senior Counsel who stated that the Officer who issued the notice, has a responsibility to enquire on the representation made, come to a subjective satisfaction and therefore, an onus is cast on that particular Officer to pass necessary orders with respect to notice issued by him/her on considering the representation received from the person/company to whom the notice had been issued.
13.In
this connection

, the learned Senior Counsel relied on a judgment of the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gullapalli Nageswara Rao and others Vs. Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation and another reported in AIR 1959 SC 308, wherein, it had been M/S.S.M.Mohammed Ibrahim & Co. Private ... vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 20 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63832338/
4 stated that if an officer who issues a notice does not examine the representation given, and on such notice, another officer passes an order adverse to the interest of the person to whom the notice had been issued, then such order suffers.

sentences.text:
It had been held as follows:
31.The

second objection is that while the Act and the Rules framed thereunder impose a duty on the State Government to give a personal hearing, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis procedure prescribed by the Rules impose a duty on the Secretary to hear and the Chief Minister to decide.
This divided responsibility is destructive of the concept of Judicial hearing.
If one person hears and another decides, then personal hearing becomes an empty formality.
We therefore hold that the said procedure followed in this case also offends another basic principle of judicial procedure.
14.That one limited point alone has to be re-examined by the respondents.
On that basis, the impugned orders are set aside.

However, liberty is given either to the Officer, who passed the impugned order, namely, the Commissioner of Food Safety to issue notice if he has necessary authority to issue notice, receive representation and pass an order or the Designated Officer, Tamil Nadu Food Safety Department to issue notice, receive representation and pass necessary orders.
The officers may proceed in manner known to law.
15.It is stated that it would be appropriate if an opportunity of personal hearing is given before examining the facts and circumstances.
The Officer, who issues the notice may take a decision whether such notice requires personal hearing or not.
If such decision is taken he/she shall give an o p p o r t u n i t y f o r p e r s o n a l h e a r i n g a n d p r o c e e d i n m a n n e r k n o w n t o l a w .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
16.With the said observations
, this Writ Petition is allowed.

But, allowing this Writ Petition does not absolve the petitioner herein, of the fact that the product, which is manufactured cannot be screened away from the purview of the Regulations of Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales) Regulations 2011.
